answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with delayed payouts plus public fraud bounties: earnings sit in escrow for several epochs, and any peer can publish evidence that is crystal clear that an identity copied work, shared a cipher, or ran a farm of lookalikes cloaked in sable. A proven challenge slashes the escrow and pays the challenger a bounty from it. Honest agents lose nothing but time, while an attacker must keep every fake identity clean under continuous public scrutiny - one exposed identity forfeits its escrow and flags its whole farm, so farming scales losses, not profits.
